subject: RFP follow-up: Drawdown-style commit and overage mechanics
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novamed.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novamed.com, Jared Klein <jared.klein@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-08-21T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: RFP question: drawdown-style commit mechanics

Tessa — thanks for the detailed RFP response. Procurement had one commercial question we need clarified before the TOC review Friday:

We prefer a drawdown (pre-paid) commit model where NovaMed deposits a committed token balance that gets consumed across workloads. Can you confirm the following points in writing:
- Do committed drawdowns expire month-to-month or can unused committed tokens roll forward for the contract year?
- How do overages bill if drawdown is exhausted mid-month (immediate per-token billing vs pooled monthly true-up)?
- Are burst/buffer credits available for sudden spikes and how are they priced relative to the commit rate?

If you can provide a short worked example with our expected monthly baseline (approx. 450M tokens/month) and a 20% burst cushion, that will help procurement finalize the SOW.

Thanks — Elena
Senior Sourcing Manager
NovaMed Health Systems

------
Elena Soto
On Mon, Aug 21, 2028 at 09:14 AM "",
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novamed.com>
Cc: Jared Klein <jared.klein@novamed.com>, procurement@novamed.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-21T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RFP question: drawdown-style commit mechanics

Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Summarizing our proposed drawdown (pre-pay) commercial construct and a short worked example below. I’m attaching a term sheet and the compute estimate workbook. High level first, then the numbers.

Key commercial constructs (summary):
- Commit Pool: NovaMed prepays a committed token pool that is usable across models and routes. Unused committed tokens roll forward month-to-month within the contract year (12-month smoothing). At contract year end unused committed tokens are eligible for a one-time true-up credit or can be rolled into an optional renewal bucket (mutually agreed).
- Overages: If the drawdown is exhausted mid-month, additional consumption is billed at the published overage rate for the billing period. We offer two overage paths: immediate pay-as-you-go per-token rates, or an optional auto-top-up to a pre-agreed burst cushion (see below). All overages are consolidated on the monthly invoice unless you elect daily billing for high-frequency reconciliation.
- Burst Cushion: We can provision an optional burst cushion equal to a percentage of your committed monthly average (e.g., 20%). Pricing for the cushion is discounted relative to on-demand overage: it is priced at 75% of the published overage rate and is reserved capacity that you can consume during spikes. Unconsumed cushion tokens expire monthly (unless you elect to convert consumed cushion into true unpaid overage charges).
- True-up cadence & credits: Monthly invoicing with quarterly reconciliation. If actual consumption over the quarter falls below committed drawdown amortized volume, we will issue a credit equal to the unused committed tokens valued at the contracted commit rate; conversely, over-consumption beyond commit + cushion is charged at overage rates.
- Cancellation & pro-rata: Early termination allows for pro-rata refund of remaining committed token value less a 10% early-termination administrative fee, invoiced on final settlement.

Worked example (NovaMed baseline ~450M tokens/month):
- Annual commit: 5,400M tokens (450M * 12). We price this at the Tier2 commit rate (model-weighted blended price) — see attached term sheet.
- Monthly amortized drawdown: 450M tokens (automatically applied from the prepaid pool).
- 20% burst cushion: 90M tokens/month reserved; priced at 75% of on-demand overage.
- Scenario: Month X consumption = 560M tokens (24% above baseline). Billing sequence: first 450M consumed from monthly amortized drawdown, next 90M consumed from burst cushion, remaining 20M billed at overage rate on that month’s invoice.

Example dollar math (illustrative only — see term sheet for firm rates):
- Commit blended rate (Tier2): $0.0008 per token -> monthly commit cost = 450M * $0.0008 = $360,000 (prepaid annually or amortized monthly).
- Burst cushion price (75% of overage; overage = $0.0012/token) -> cushion price = $0.0009/token -> 90M * $0.0009 = $81,000 (reserved monthly premium).
- Overage: 20M * $0.0012 = $24,000.
- Net for Month X (when cushion used): $360,000 (commit amortized) + $81,000 (cushion) + $24,000 (overage) = $465,000.

Attachments:
- Redwood_Commercial_TermSheet_Q3_2028.pdf (term-level pricing bands, model weight table, billing samples)
- nova_compute_estimate.xlsx (workbook with token split by model class and monthly profiles)

Operational notes:
- Model weighting: we provide a model-weighted token calculator; committed token consumption applies to raw token counts, and the invoice uses model weights to map to compute tiers for pricing.
- Rollover guardrails: roll-forward only within contract year; any remaining tokens at year-end can be credited or rolled into renewal at a negotiated discount.

Next steps: if this aligns with NovaMed’s procurement intent, we propose:
1) We send a redline-friendly term sheet and a sample invoice layout (attached).
2) Procurement confirms whether they want the burst cushion as a reserved monthly charge or prefer pure on-demand overages.
3) If reserved cushion accepted, Redwood will provision the cushion and flag alerting thresholds in the Console for cost/runaway protection.

Happy to hop on a 30m call tomorrow for the TOC prep.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jared Klein <jared.klein@novamed.com>

Date: 2028-08-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RFP question: drawdown-style commit mechanics

Tessa — quick follow-up from procurement: two clarifications before we sign off to legal:
1) Can the burst cushion be charged as a one-time monthly reservation (i.e., priced and invoiced each month regardless of use), or do you only invoice the cushion when it is consumed? Which option gives NovaMed the best blended unit economics?
2) For the year-end true-up credit, is the credit issued at the original commit price (so NovaMed recovers the dollar value) or at on-demand rates? Procurement prefers recovering the original committed dollar value.

If you can confirm those two points in writing we can move to TOC/legal.

Thanks — Jared
Director, Cloud Economics
NovaMed
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Klein <jared.klein@novamed.com>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@novamed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-22T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RFP question: drawdown-style commit mechanics

Jared — good questions. Short answers then one operational note.

1) Cushion invoicing options: we support both modes.
   - Reserved-monthly billing (recommended for budgeting): the cushion is invoiced monthly as a reservation fee (you pay the cushion premium every month regardless of use). This provides predictable blended economics and guarantees capacity for spikes.
   - On-consume billing: the cushion is billed only when consumed at the cushion price. This minimizes wasted spend if spikes are rare, but gives less predictable monthly spend.

   Blended economics: reserved-monthly billing typically yields a slightly lower effective per-token cost when cushions are used frequently because the reserved fee is amortized across many consumed cushion tokens. If NovaMed expects sustained spikes (20% sustained), we recommend reserved-monthly for predictability and slightly better blended pricing.

2) Year-end true-up credit valuation: we will credit unused committed token value at the original committed price (not at on-demand). That preserves NovaMed’s committed dollar recovery and is consistent with standard commit accounting.

Operational note: we can include an optional rollover-to-renewal clause where an agreed percentage of unused tokens (e.g., up to 15%) can auto-roll into the renewal bucket at the same commit rate if NovaMed signs a renewal within 60 days — this is a negotiation point for the TOC.

If that looks good I’ll ask Legal to prepare the TOC with the reservation option explicitly described and the year-end credit language included. We can also mark the HubSpot deal as ‘TOC ready’ and send DocuSign once legal has the redline.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: internal: approval to offer reserved cushion vs on-consume guidance

Tessa — quick internal: I reviewed the numbers. Given NovaMed’s profile (steady baseline + periodic campaigns) we should encourage reserved-monthly cushion. A few reasons: 1) it protects their app from sudden throttling, 2) increases AR and retention, 3) gives us forecasting certainty for capacity.

I approve offering the reserved-monthly cushion at 75% of on-demand overage as you proposed, but only if we keep the rollover cap at 15% and include a 60-day renewal window to move unused tokens into a renewal bucket at commit price. Also fine with the year-end credit at commit price.

Rishi — please prepare a sample invoice template with the reserved cushion option and the quarterly true-up lines. Aditya — add an alert profile for Console to trigger at 85% and 95% of monthly amortized usage and for cushion consumption so we can proactively notify NovaMed.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novamed.com>, Jared Klein <jared.klein@novamed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-25T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RFP question: drawdown-style commit mechanics — confirmed

Elena / Jared — following internal sign-off: confirmed and ready to include in the TOC.

Summary of confirmed points for the TOC (final):
- Commit drawdown: prepaid annual pool, month-to-month roll-forward within contract year; year-end credit at commit price or optional roll into renewal (up to 15% rollover cap).
- Overages: billed at agreed overage rates when commit + cushion exhausted; monthly consolidated invoice; daily billing available on request.
- Burst cushion: supported as reserved-monthly (invoiced monthly regardless of use) or on-consume. Reserved-monthly recommended and approved at 75% of published overage.
- True-up & credits: monthly invoicing with quarterly reconciliation; credits issued at original commit price.
- Termination: pro-rata refund less 10% admin fee.

Next steps: I’ll send the redline-friendly term sheet to procurement and share a sample invoice + Console alert plan. Expect DocuSign link once Legal completes the TOC — targeting by end of week.

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Commercial_TermSheet_Q3_2028.pdf (attached), nova_compute_estimate.xlsx (attached)

Happy to jump on the TOC prep call tomorrow at 10:00 PT if you’d like.

Best —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
